found_values.value: Thresholds: INA3221 critical 30.00 mV (3.0 A on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, each single conversion); warning 10.00 mV (1.0 A, 250 counts, averaged value, AVG 4); INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV (24,000 counts of 1.25 uV, ADCRANGE 1) on both paths. Latching: INA3221 critical and warning transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state), because the main coprocessor times the lines and only a Mask/Enable read on the measurement coprocessor's bus clears a latch; INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm. Blanking time: not read. SBOS576C states when the transparent Critical pin pulls low (7.3.2.1) and not when it releases with three channels enabled; its only example enables CH1 alone (9.2.1, Table 9-1). If the pin holds until the same channel converts again, 5 ms lies between one refresh (3.63 ms max) and two (6.6 ms typ) and the abort fires; if the pin follows each conversion of any channel, a sustained overcurrent on one channel holds the line low about 1.1 ms in each 3.3 ms and no blanking above 1.21 ms fires. A bench measurement of the Critical pin with three channels enabled and one above the limit, or TI's statement, fixes it. Against the breaker: the blanking acts on 3.0 to 3.96 A only; from 3.96 to 4.84 A the port switch's breaker acts (owner)
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113, :387, :389; docs/Servo.md:35-36; INA3221 SBOS576C 6.5, 7.3.2.1, 7.3.2.2, 9.2.1, 9.2.2, Mask/Enable register bits 10 and 11, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf; INA228 SLYS021A Table 7-16, 7.6.1.13; FU-2H adjudicator rulings 016 and 017

SBOS576C states that the transparent Critical pin pulls low when any channel's conversion exceeds its limit (7.3.2.1) and not when it releases with three channels enabled; its example enables CH1 alone (9.2.1, Table 9-1). Reading A, the pin holds until the same channel converts again: 5 ms lies between one refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100: 3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max) and two (6.6 ms typ; no minimum conversion time stated), a single over-limit conversion is logged, two abort. Reading B, the pin follows each conversion of any channel: a sustained overcurrent on one channel holds the line low about 1.1 ms in each 3.3 ms and no blanking above 1.21 ms ever aborts. Fixed by a bench measurement of the Critical pin with three channels enabled and one above the limit, or by TI's statement. Until then the owner's blanking rule on the critical line is not shown to abort a sustained 3.0 to 3.96 A overcurrent; the firmware check at every 5 ms sample on the measurement coprocessor still does
